A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GAP-MLLM. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original grounding, captioning, detection, reconstruction, and ablation results in Sections 4 and 7, with qualitative results in Section 8.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds corruption robustness, small-object evaluation, and qualitative outdoor detection results in Sections 7.3–7.5.

M1.justification: Section 7.5 introduces sliding-window inference for dynamic videos, processing each window independently in its first-frame coordinate system. The encoders, gated fusion, joint pre-training, and two-stage grounding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond the retained indoor datasets to degraded first-frame inputs and dynamic outdoor driving scenes from nuScenes. The outdoor evaluation is qualitative only, but introduces a substantially different domain and scene conditions.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. The new small-object analysis uses VG-LLM, already evaluated for detection. Table 3 relabels the larger VG-LLM row from 7B to 8B with identical scores; this is a reported model-size revision rather than an established new comparison method.

E3.justification: New protocols corrupt only the first frame using blur at sigma 8/12 or occlusion covering 30%/50%, and report category-specific and averaged metrics for eight small-object classes. Table 3 also revises the stated VG-LLM size from 7B to 8B without establishing reruns. Existing training budgets, splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections 7.3–7.5 substantially expand supplementary analysis: sensitivity to first-frame corruption, small-object performance under patch merging, and qualitative dynamic-scene/domain-shift testing. Existing component, fusion, supervision, and grounding ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing reconstruction mean/median summaries are unchanged, and the new tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries are retained, but new results substantially broaden the findings. Table 15 reports F1 declining from 50.6 on clean inputs to 47.5/46.0 under blur and 50.1/48.4 under occlusion. Table 16 reports small-object average F1 of 31.2 versus VG-LLM's 16.0, and Figure 12 adds qualitative outdoor detections. These are additional conditions, not improved scores on the original benchmarks.

T1.justification: The token definitions, fusion equations (1)–(3), and coordinate formulations are unchanged. No mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about activating geometric priors through sparse joint pre-training and multi-level gated fusion. The appendix extensions do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: The added analyses interpret corruption tolerance as effective multi-frame aggregation and small-object performance as preservation of information after patch merging. Section 7.5 newly states the static-scene assumption, attributes preliminary outdoor generalization to VGGT priors, and acknowledges missing motion modeling and temporal association. Section 9's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page address, specifies that the existing ten-scene reconstruction evaluation uses random ScanNet scenes, and documents corruption settings and window-based inference. The random-scene statement is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed sampling. The PDFs do not establish code availability through the new address.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to nuScenes and Li et al.'s work on causal tracing of object representations. All 61 earlier references are retained, and the positioning relative to geometric reconstruction and prior 3D MLLMs remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and terminology edits, updates affiliation and author-note text, adds acknowledgments, and inserts Sections 7.3–7.5 within the existing supplementary structure. The main narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Tables 15–16 and Figures 10–12 substantially expand the appendix's visual presentation of robustness, small objects, and dynamic scenes. Figure 11 redisplays detections already shown in Figure 7 with enlarged crops. Original appendix Figures 10–12 are retained as Figures 13–15 and relocated. Smaller teaser, architecture-label, and front-matter layout edits also occur.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful quantitative checks of first-frame corruption and small-object detection, plus an explicit qualification about motion modeling. These strengthen assessment of robustness and applicability while retaining the original evidence. The benefit is limited because the outdoor demonstration remains qualitative and the small-object comparison does not directly isolate the effect of patch merging.
